name: RevisionLedger
what_it_holds: Small Python bitemporal-ledger library (valid time + system/knowledge time per data point) demonstrated on ALFRED's Real GDP series (GDPC1), with two real sample vintages of Q4-2023 US real GDP committed as fixtures with SHA-256 manifests. 16 passing tests, MIT, 0 stars, 14 commits -- proof-of-concept scope, explicitly not a general downloader yet.
why_useful: A tiny, clean reference implementation of 'as-of' querying for macro vintages (exactly this theme), but scope is currently limited to a worked example, not a usable general tool yet.
time_coverage: single worked example (Q4 2023 GDP, two vintages)
themes: Point-in-time macro vintages: ALFRED tooling, Philly Fed real-time dataset, ONS revisions, Eurostat vintages; packages for vintage-aware backtests
why_all: A tiny, clean reference implementation of 'as-of' querying for macro vintages (exactly this theme), but scope is currently limited to a worked example, not a usable general tool yet.

name: vintage (as-of statistics query tool)
what_it_holds: Single-file Python/SQLite CLI tool (vintage.py) that ingests generic CSV releases (series_id, period, released_at, value) and supports 'as-of' snapshots and 'diff' comparisons between two knowledge dates; preserves source text so trivial revisions (1.0 -> 1.00) aren't lost. MIT, 1 commit, 0 stars -- generic, source-agnostic, user must supply their own release CSVs (no bundled data).
why_useful: Generic point-in-time query tool that could sit on top of any macro series the team already scrapes with a release timestamp (e.g. consensus snapshots, FRED pulls) to do as-of queries without building custom code; very early/minimal though.
themes: Point-in-time macro vintages: ALFRED tooling, Philly Fed real-time dataset, ONS revisions, Eurostat vintages; packages for vintage-aware backtests
why_all: Generic point-in-time query tool that could sit on top of any macro series the team already scrapes with a release timestamp (e.g. consensus snapshots, FRED pulls) to do as-of queries without building custom code; very early/minimal though.

name: census-api-datasets
what_it_holds: Tracks additions/removals of datasets on the Census Bureau's API over time (a changelog/registry, 15 stars) — i.e., a curated index of what's available and when it appeared or disappeared from the API.
why_useful: Metadata tool for discovering new/deprecated Census series systematically rather than manually; low direct KPI value but useful for a future systematic scan of Census offerings relevant to travel/housing.
themes: FRED / BEA / BLS / Census API clients and curated macro panels (consumer sentiment, PCE services, CPI lodging, airfares, unemployment by metro)
why_all: Metadata tool for discovering new/deprecated Census series systematically rather than manually; low direct KPI value but useful for a future systematic scan of Census offerings relevant to travel/housing.

name: Rdatasets
what_it_holds: Mirror of 3,648 datasets originally bundled inside R packages, exported as CSV and Parquet with an HTML/CSV index; broad general-purpose collection (economics, social science, biology, etc.), not macro-specific but includes many economic/time-series teaching datasets.
why_useful: Worth a targeted grep of its CSV index for any macro/travel/tourism/airfare series bundled from lesser-known R packages (e.g. AER, Ecdat, wooldridge) that might not otherwise surface; low direct hit rate but essentially free to check.
license: GPL-3.0 (code); data licensing uncertain per maintainer's own disclosure
themes: FRED / BEA / BLS / Census API clients and curated macro panels (consumer sentiment, PCE services, CPI lodging, airfares, unemployment by metro)
why_all: Worth a targeted grep of its CSV index for any macro/travel/tourism/airfare series bundled from lesser-known R packages (e.g. AER, Ecdat, wooldridge) that might not otherwise surface; low direct hit rate but essentially free to check.

name: ud4yfr/bnpl-stress-test
what_it_holds: Monte Carlo stress-test model comparing Affirm vs Klarna unit economics under rising delinquency scenarios. Appears to be a modeling exercise (parametrized assumptions), not a committed real-data extract of Affirm/Klarna disclosed statistics. Updated 1 Aug 2026, 0 stars, no license listed.
why_useful: Marginal: illustrates how BNPL delinquency sensitivity could be modeled, but does not appear to hold real disclosed Affirm/Klarna public stats (10-Q GMV, delinquency rates) that would be the actual high-value target; would need inspection of source code to confirm any embedded real figures.
themes: Consumer credit and BNPL: Klarna/Affirm public stats, Fed G.19, credit card delinquency, CFPB complaints dataset (Airbnb refund complaints), BBB complaint scrapers
why_all: Marginal: illustrates how BNPL delinquency sensitivity could be modeled, but does not appear to hold real disclosed Affirm/Klarna public stats (10-Q GMV, delinquency rates) that would be the actual high-value target; would need inspection of source code to confirm any embedded real figures.
